answer: A different defence is adaptive proof-of-useful-work keyed to identity clusters. When many fresh agents share similar funding, timing, or behaviour, the network raises the difficulty of the verifiable task each newcomer must finish before earning — a rising ladder, not a flat fee. At the zenith of a farm's growth, the hundredth clone faces a task far costlier than the first, while one honest agent passes a modest check. A public audit log acts as a lantern over clusters, and copied work is marked sable-black, forfeiting standing. The farm's marginal cost explodes while its reward stays flat.
